Plot a myDAR walk

Source: R/mydar_views.R
mydar_views.Rd

Each function turns one part of a mydar_walk (from read_mydar_walk or mydar_iphone_walk) into a myIO chart.

Usage

mydar_plan_view(walk, profile = NULL, points = NULL, height = "460px")

mydar_orthophoto_view(walk, height = "460px")

mydar_terrain_view(
  walk,
  hillshade = TRUE,
  azimuth = 315,
  altitude = 45,
  height = "420px"
)

mydar_profile(walk, from = NULL, to = NULL, width = 0.5)

mydar_profile_view(walk, from = NULL, to = NULL, width = 0.5, height = "360px")

mydar_trajectory_view(walk, height = "320px")

mydar_sigma_view(walk, height = "320px")

mydar_accuracy_view(walk, height = "320px")

mydar_gps_view(walk, height = "320px")

Arguments

walk

A mydar_walk.

profile

Optional list(from = c(x, y), to = c(x, y)); draws the profile line on the plan view.

points

Draw the points, colored by class, over the orthophoto, small and translucent so the image shows through. Defaults to TRUE only when the walk has no orthophoto. Brushing the plan view selects these points, so turn them on to link it to a profile.

height

Widget height, a CSS size.

hillshade

If TRUE (default), shade the DEM by a hillshade lit from azimuth (degrees clockwise from north) and altitude (degrees above the horizon).

azimuth, altitude

Hillshade light direction.

from, to

Profile line ends, each c(x, y) in the walk's coordinates. When both are NULL, the line crosses the track at its midpoint and spans the point cloud.

width

Corridor width in meters; points within width / 2 of the line are kept.

Value

A myIO widget. mydar_profile() returns the corridor points as a data frame with distance (meters along the line), offset (meters left of the line, negative to the right), and the point columns.

Details

mydar_plan_view()

The walk from above: the orthophoto with the track, point features and, when profile is given, the profile line on it, drawn to scale (equal meters per pixel on both axes) with the walk's Shape and Map accuracy as a caption. Points colored by LAS class are an optional overlay (points).

mydar_orthophoto_view()

The orthophoto alone, to scale, with the track.

mydar_terrain_view()

The DEM as a "raster" layer, colored by height and, by default, shaded by a hillshade, to scale.

mydar_profile_view()

Points within width of the line from from to to, plotted as height against distance along the line, with the DEM height along the same line.

mydar_trajectory_view()

The 95% map-position radius along the walk over time, with each GPS fix's reported horizontal accuracy.

mydar_sigma_view()

The distribution of per-point sigma_m (1-sigma per axis) for LiDAR and camera points, on a log10 axis because camera sigma can be a hundred times LiDAR's.

mydar_accuracy_view()

The accuracy table's 95% figures: shape (how well distances within the walk hold, by range band) against map position (where the walk sits on the map), and held-out pin misses when the walk used pins.

mydar_gps_view()

Each GPS fix's residual against the fused track, with the 95% residual the processing expected.

See also

mydar_dashboard lays out all of these at once.

Examples

walk <- mydar_iphone_walk
mydar_plan_view(walk)


mydar_orthophoto_view(walk)


mydar_terrain_view(walk)


mydar_profile_view(walk)


mydar_trajectory_view(walk)


mydar_sigma_view(walk)


mydar_accuracy_view(walk)


head(mydar_profile(walk))

# mydar_gps_view() needs GPS fixes with residuals; this walk has none.
if (any(is.finite(walk$gps_fixes$residual_m))) mydar_gps_view(walk)
